newsitem.title: HUNGARY: BELGIAN, BRITISH AND IRISH CITIES WIN BEAUTY PRIZE.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN, BRITISH AND IRISH CITIES WIN BEAUTY PRIZE.

text.p: Europe's three most beautiful cities are in Belgium, Britain and Ireland, an international jury decided on Saturday.
Malmedy, Barnstaple and Skerries have each won a golden award at the European competition of towns and villages in bloom, held in Eger, north-eastern Hungary, a former winner of the annual contest.
"I am absolutely thrilled. We have all worked very hard," the head of Barnstaple's district council, Faye Webber told Reuters, hugging the prize, an eight-kilo bronze plate with golden flowers.

The crowded ceremony hall of Eger's 18th century baroque university proved to be a setting of matching splendor for the approximately 300 guests from nine European countries waiting for this year's winners to be announced.
"Having the chance to host this event is a prize in itself," said Ilona David, professor of Eger university.
The three-day event gave guests to have a taste not only of the city's beauty, but of its wines as well, in the nearby Valley of Beautiful Women.

Despite an unseasonably chilly September weekend the warm and friendly athmosphere of the gathering reached its climax as the winners were announced in four languages and took their turn on the podium to tote the plaques.
But the lucky winners also remembered all those who contributed to their cities' victory.
"Everybody in the town is to be congratulated on the great work that they all did," said Maeve McGann of voluntary organisation Skerries Tidy Town Committee.
